podcast.body: Daniel Lopatin, operating under the alias Chuck Person, released this collection of his earlier works in 2010. The album built upon his initial YouTube experiments, further developing the Eccojams style by presenting popular song extracts reduced in tempo and pitch, and assembled in loops. This release was foundational for the early vaporwave scene. "Al año siguiente, el mismo Lopatín publicó una colección de esos trabajos a los cañadio otros, bajolálias de Chuck Person en Chuck Person Seco-Jumps volumen 1."

srcs.episode: Vaporwave: Mucho más que un Meme

podcast.body: This album, released under the alias Chuck Person, is credited with practically creating the vaporwave genre. Lopatin manipulated fragments of existing songs, cutting, chopping, and slowing them down to transform the music into something entirely new. "Chuck Person, Seco Yams Volumen 1 en 2010, el disco que prácticamente creó el vaporwave."

srcs.episode: ¿Por qué el Slowed & Reverb y los Speed Up están rompiendo YT y TikTok?

podcast.title: Creative Manipulation
podcast.body: Through this album, Daniel Lopatin skillfully manipulated songs by artists like Michael Jackson, Kate Bush, and Tupac. By altering their fragments, he managed to imbue them with a different, more evocative, and nostalgic sentiment and tone, laying the groundwork for the vaporwave aesthetic. "Manipulando canciones de Michael Jackson, Kate Bush o TuPak, conseguía darles un sentimiento y un tono diferente, más evocador y nostálgico."
